Plot feeding level

Source: R/plots.R
plotevoFeeding.Rd

Plots the feeding level of species against body size.

Usage

plotevoFeeding(
  object,
  time_range = max(as.numeric(dimnames(object@n)$time)),
  species = TRUE,
  start = 1000,
  every = 1000,
  print_it = TRUE,
  returnData = FALSE,
  save_it = FALSE,
  nameSave = "Feeding.png"
)

Arguments

object

An object of class mizer::MizerSim.

time_range

The time range (either a vector of values, a vector of min and max time, or a single value) to average the abundances over. Default is the entire simulation time range.

species

Plot only a specific species and its phenotypes. Default is NULL.

start

Initial time index if plotting series.

every

Step interval if plotting series.

print_it

A boolean value that displays the plot. Default is TRUE.

returnData

A boolean value that controls the output. Either a dataframe ready for ggplot (TRUE) or the plot itself (FALSE). Default is FALSE.

save_it

A boolean value to save the plot. Default is FALSE.

nameSave

File name for saving the plot. Default is "Biomass.png".

Value

A ggplot object, or data frame if returnData = TRUE.

See also

mizer::plotting_functions

Other plotting functions: plotDynamics(), plotPredMort(), plotPredRate(), plotSS(), plotSpawn(), plotStarvation(), plotevoGrowth(), plotevoMortality(), plotevoTrait()

Examples

# \donttest{
params <- evoParams(no_sp = 5)
#> ℹ No `a` column so using a = 0.01 in w = a l^b, with w in g and l in cm.
#> ℹ No `b` column so using the isometric default b = 3 in w = a l^b.
#> ℹ Using f0, h, lambda, kappa and the predation kernel to calculate gamma.
#> Warning: Some column names in your species parameter data frame are very close to standard parameter names: `zeta` (did you mean `beta`?). Please check for mis-spellings.
sim <- evoProject(params, t_max = 20)
plotevoFeeding(sim)

# }
